title: Which Way Does the E Point?

patient.name: Mdm Ong Geok Choo
patient.presenting_complaint: Here for a routine eye check; speaks only Hokkien and cannot read English letters

history.hpc: Mdm Ong is brought in by her daughter for a routine eye check. She has mild blurring of vision but no pain, redness, or sudden change. Her daughter explains: 'My mother only speak Hokkien, she don't know how to read the English letters one.' Mdm Ong is cooperative but cannot use a standard letter chart. A suitable testing method is needed to obtain an accurate VA.
history.pmhx: Hypertension, well controlled. No previous eye surgery.
history.social_hx: Lives with her daughter. Dialect-speaking, did not attend formal schooling. Non-smoker.

examination_findings.anterior_segment: Early lens changes both eyes; cornea clear, no redness

investigations.va_distance: Standard letter charts not suitable as the patient cannot read English letters. The E chart (tumbling E) was used: the patient indicates the direction the legs of the 'E' point (up/down/left/right) by hand or by pointing. RE 6/12, LE 6/9. Pinhole applied to the right eye (VA 6/12 threshold) with slight improvement.
investigations.pinhole: RE: slight improvement with pinhole, suggesting a partly refractive component.
investigations.iop_nct: RE 16 mmHg, LE 15 mmHg — normal range.

diagnosis: Mild reduction of vision, measured reliably using the E chart given the language barrier. The E chart is appropriate for patients who cannot read letters (young children, those who are illiterate, or non-English speakers). Slight pinhole improvement suggests a refractive component. For doctor review.

immediate: Recognise that a standard letter chart is unsuitable and select the E chart (tumbling E) for this patient
Use the daughter to interpret and demonstrate the task: show how to indicate the direction the 'E' points
Test the right eye first, occluding the other eye, with hand hygiene and an alcohol-wiped occluder
Apply pinhole as VA is at the 6/12 threshold and document any improvement
Perform NCT for IOP in both eyes
Document the chart used (E chart), VA for each eye, pinhole result, and IOP for the doctor
follow_up: Doctor to perform a comprehensive assessment including fundus examination
Consider refraction given the slight pinhole improvement
Arrange interpreter support for future visits if needed
patient_education: Use the daughter to explain the test simply and reassure Mdm Ong
Explain that the E chart lets us measure her vision accurately even without reading letters
Reassure that her eye pressures are normal and the vision is only mildly reduced
Explain the next step is a doctor review

key_points: Identifies the language barrier and that the patient cannot read English letters
Establishes the visual complaint is mild and without red flags (pain, redness, sudden loss)
Engages the accompanying daughter appropriately as an interpreter
Selects the E chart (tumbling E) as the appropriate chart for a non-English-speaking patient
Explains and demonstrates the task clearly (indicating the direction the E points)
Tests right eye first with proper hygiene, and applies pinhole at the 6/12 threshold
Performs and documents NCT for IOP
Understands when the E chart is indicated (children, illiterate, non-English speakers)
Obtains a reliable VA despite the language barrier
Interprets slight pinhole improvement as a possible refractive component
Defers comprehensive assessment to the doctor
Documents the chart used (E chart), VA for each eye, pinhole result, and IOP clearly
Communicates with the patient via the daughter in a respectful, reassuring way
Recognises the need for interpreter support at future visits
Hands over to the doctor with a clear summary
